status.COMPLETE: Traced end to end in the current source and covered by a test or a live proof. Not 'a page exists'.
status.FINISH: Real implementation exists but a named part of it is missing. The missing part is in next_action.
status.CONSOLIDATE: Two or more implementations answer the same question and can drift apart.
status.REMOVE: Code with no caller. Delete it or give it a caller - a decision, not a cleanup.
status.POLICY_REQUIRED: The code is correct and deliberately refuses to act until a human decides. Nobody has decided.
status.BLOCKED: Cannot proceed without something outside this repository.
status.NOT_BUILT: No implementation found. Searched, not assumed.

how_to_read.priority: P0 stop-the-world, P1 next, P2 soon, P3 whenever
how_to_read.completed_on: null unless a commit or a dated document proves it. Never guessed.
how_to_read.previously_missed: true = this was NOT on any earlier roadmap and is being added now, openly.

items.title: POST /leads/demo-request is registered twice; the second handler is unreachable
items.evidence: leads_router.py:1729 @router.post('/demo-request') -> create_demo_request(DemoRequestCreate) and leads_router.py:2153 @router.post('/demo-request') -> demo_request(DemoRequestPayload). FastAPI matches the first registration, so create_demo_request always wins and demo_request never runs. The OPTIONS preflight at :2147 belongs to the second one and still answers, so a browser preflight succeeds and the POST then lands on a handler with a different schema.
items.notes: The shadowed handler is the one that emails LEAD_NOTIFY_EMAILS. If the marketing site posts the second schema, the live handler rejects it with 422 and nobody is notified. This is the public demo-request path from bookaboost.live.
items.decision_required: Which handler is the intended one?
items.next_action: Check what bookaboost.live actually posts and what it has been receiving back, keep one handler, delete the other, and add a test asserting only one route is registered for this path.

items.title: Public demo requests resolve their organization by name match with an arbitrary fallback
items.evidence: leads_router.py create_demo_request: Organization.name.ilike('%bookaboost%') and, failing that, db.query(Organization).first()
items.notes: This is fuzzy organization resolution on a public, unauthenticated write path, and the fallback drops a real inbound lead into whatever organization happens to be returned first. Renaming a brand silently redirects public leads; the fallback can put a stranger's contact details into a customer's workspace.
items.decision_required: Which organization owns marketing-site demo requests?
items.next_action: Resolve by a durable configured organization id. If it is unset, refuse the request and log it - never fall back to an arbitrary row.

items.system: CRM, Case Files, Reporting & Platform Health
items.title: CRM connection API keys are stored in plaintext in a column named api_key_encrypted
items.evidence: app/models/models.py:1672 api_key_encrypted = Column(String); crm_router.py:73 '# stored as api_key_encrypted (plaintext for now)'; crm_router.py:227 updates['api_key_encrypted'] = payload.api_key; crm_service.py:98 '# stored as plaintext for now'. The platform already has the primitive and uses it: integrations/__init__.py:86-89 calls decrypt_value(config.api_key_encrypted).
items.notes: No exposure route was found - the value is not returned to any client - so this is not a P0. The column name is the real hazard: anyone reading the schema will believe these are encrypted.
items.next_action: Encrypt on write with the existing helper, decrypt on read, migrate existing rows, and add a test asserting the stored bytes are not the plaintext key. Never log the value.
